sections.h2: Who does what on a Genesee County tax bill?
sections.html:
Three layers share the work. A city or township assessor values each parcel, a local treasurer collects the current bill, and the county treasurer steps in once the balance is overdue on March 1. In between, the county equalization office audits the local assessors so that values stay comparable across the county.

The county was created on March 28, 1835 and organized on April 4, 1836. Flint is the seat, and 33 cities, townships and villages sit on 636.94 square miles of land. The eleven cities are Burton, Clio, Davison, Fenton (partly in the county), Flint, Flushing, Grand Blanc, Linden, Montrose, Mount Morris and Swartz Creek. Gaines, Goodrich, Lennon, Otisville and Otter Lake are villages. Your parcel's municipality decides which assessor and local treasurer you call.

Flint is carved out of one county service. Equalization maintains property descriptions for every municipality but Flint, whose own assessor keeps those records.

sections.h2: Which county desks matter, and where are they?
sections.html:
Three county offices fit this topic, all inside the county administration building on South Saginaw Street in Flint. The equalization page points owners to the city or township for assessments and current bills, and to the county only for delinquent ones.

  • Equalization, Suite 8B: (810) 257-3017. It writes the annual equalization report and the millage reduction report.
  • Treasurer, Suite 2A, 324 S Saginaw St: (810) 257-3054, weekdays from 8:00 to 4:00. It takes delinquent payments and runs tax foreclosure. Partial payments are encouraged, by mail, online or through an automated line at 1-877-805-2856, and the online and phone routes add a fee.
  • Clerk and Register of Deeds, Suite 1A: records deeds and mortgages. See the separate register of deeds guide for its fees and transfer tax.

The equalization page also links State Tax Commission Bulletin 11 of 2025, which lays out the 2026 property tax, collections and equalization calendar.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Genesee County housing?
sections.html:
With 401,093 residents in the 2025 estimate, Genesee ranks fifth among Michigan counties and has lost 1.3% since the April 2020 base. It counts 167,334 households and 185,007 housing units, and owners live in 70.7% of occupied homes.

  • Median home value: $182,400 for 2020-2024.
  • Monthly ownership cost: $1,455 with a mortgage, $583 without.
  • Median gross rent: $989.
  • Median household income: $62,281.
  • Building permits in 2025: 444.

The county grew from 22,498 people in 1860 to 211,641 in 1930, reached 450,449 in 1980 and counted 406,211 in 2020. Bishop International Airport and the Flint Amtrak station, which also serves intercity buses, tie the county to the rest of the state. Bills follow those values, so a Flint homeowner, where the median is $53,500, sees a very different tax picture from a Grand Blanc one. The Flint River drains most of the county, and I-75, I-69, I-475 and US 23 meet near its center. Figures are from Census QuickFacts.

sections.h2: Where can a Genesee County owner contest a value?
sections.html:
At the local board of review in the owner's own city or township, then at the Michigan Tax Tribunal. The county does not hear individual appeals.

Each board convenes on the second Monday of March unless the local government shifts the first sitting to the Tuesday or Wednesday after. Over that week a board owes the public at least 12 hours, three of them after 6 p.m. Each person who protests receives written word of the outcome by the first Monday of June, with the tribunal's address and filing date. Out-of-town owners can protest by letter.

Tribunal petitions are due May 31 for commercial, industrial and developmental real property and July 31 for residential and farm property, and a residential owner must have gone to the board first. Boards also sit in July and December for qualified errors, such as a clerical slip or a wrong measurement, and for certain exemptions. Those fixes reach back only to the current and previous year.

sections.h2: How does a Genesee County bill become delinquent?
sections.html:
Whatever is still unpaid on March 1 of the year after the levy goes to the Genesee County Treasurer, which serves as the county's foreclosing unit. The schedule below comes from Michigan Treasury.

DateCounty treasurer action
March 1, year oneTakes in unpaid bills, adds a 4% fee and 1% interest each month
June 1 and September 1Sends two first-class mailings to the owner
October 1Adds a $15 fee
February 1, year twoSends certified mail to the owner and a letter to the occupant
March 1, year twoForfeits the parcel, adds a $175 title fee, starts half-percent monthly redemption interest
March 30 and 31, year threeJudgment deadline, then the last day to redeem

Reference: Michigan Treasury, Foreclosure Process Timelines.

Sales then happen online. In 2026 the county held a minimum bid auction on September 3, a re-offer round on September 25 and a no-reserve sale on October 30. A Genesee County Land Bank exists to help return foreclosed property to the tax rolls.

sections.h2: Can a former owner claim money from a foreclosure sale?
sections.html:
Sometimes. For parcels that sold at auction from 2013 to 2020 for more than the taxes and costs owed, the treasurer's page describes a class settlement, Fox v. Saginaw County. Its claims deadline, July 16, 2026, has passed.

For sales on or after July 18, 2020, an owner or lienholder files Form 5743, the Notice of Intention to Claim Interest in Foreclosure Sales Proceeds, and then a motion to claim the remaining proceeds on form CC 540. Both forms sit on the treasurer's page, along with the State Bar of Michigan referral line, 800-968-0738.

sections.h2: How does a sale close when tax is still owed in Genesee County?
sections.html:
The closing agent obtains a payoff, and the unpaid tax, interest and fees are deducted from the seller's check. If the bill has been returned to the county, the payoff comes from the county treasurer's office.

A seller also faces transfer tax. Michigan sets the state share at $3.75 per $500 and the county share at 55 cents per $500, the rate for any county under two million people. On a $180,000 sale, near this county's median home value, 360 units of $500 produce $1,350 for the state and $198 for the county, or $1,548 together. The county treasurer is paid within 15 days after the deed is delivered. Foreclosure transfers, deeds to a child or grandchild and land contracts that leave title with the seller are exempt.

Someone behind on tax, or holding a house that needs work, can sell as-is to a cash buyer and let the payoff come out at the closing.

faqs.q: Which office takes delinquent Genesee County property tax?
faqs.a: The Genesee County Treasurer, 324 S Saginaw St Ste 2A in Flint, takes payments by mail, online or phone. The counter is staffed weekdays from 8:00 to 4:00, and the online and phone options carry a fee.

faqs.q: Does the county decide what my property is worth?
faqs.a: No, the assessor of your city or township does. Equalization only checks that local assessments are comparable countywide and calculates the millage reduction report.

faqs.q: Is there a Tax Tribunal deadline for a home?
faqs.a: Yes. A residential petition is due July 31 of the tax year, after a protest at the local board. Commercial and industrial petitions are due May 31.

faqs.q: How soon can Genesee County foreclose over unpaid tax?
faqs.a: The process spans about three years. The parcel forfeits on the second March 1, a judgment must come by March 30 of year three, and March 31 is the last day to redeem.

faqs.q: What is the total transfer tax rate in Genesee County?
faqs.a: It is $4.30 per $500 of price, which is $3.75 for the state plus 55 cents for the county. The seller owes the tax and pays the county treasurer within 15 days of the deed.
